title: Grab These PlayStation Games on Disc Before They Disappear Forever!
summary:
Do you love the feeling of popping a game disc into your console? That satisfying click, the shiny cover art on your shelf — it’s a ritual many gamers treasure. But here’s a bummer: Sony says the PlayStation 5 will be the last console to use physical discs. When the PS6 arrives around 2028, games will be digital-only. That means no more discs to collect, trade, or keep forever.

But don’t panic yet! Right now, a bunch of awesome PS5 games are on sale in disc form at stores like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart. These deals are happening at the same time as the PlayStation Store’s summer sale, so you can snag physical copies for way less than usual. For example, Spider-Man 2 is just $30 — perfect if you want to swing through New York before the next game, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, comes out. Death Stranding 2, which only came out last summer, is down to $40. And even the brand-new game Saros, a wild shooter from the makers of Returnal, is discounted.

Why does this matter? Because digital games are convenient, but they’re not really yours. If a company’s servers shut down or your account gets hacked, poof — your games could vanish. A disc, on the other hand, is yours for as long as you take care of it. You can lend it to a friend, sell it, or replay it years later. With Sony planning to stop making discs in less than two years, these sales might be some of your last chances to own today’s hits on a shiny disc. So if you’re a collector — or just someone who likes to hold a game in your hands — now’s the time to grab them before they’re gone for good.
why_it_matters: If you enjoy sharing games with friends or want to keep your collection forever, grabbing discs now can protect your fun for years, because digital-only games might not be around if the companies that run them stop working.

background_read: For decades, video games came on cartridges, then CDs and Blu-ray discs. In recent years, many players download games instead, which lets companies skip manufacturing and shipping. This shift is happening across movies and music too, but for gamers who love collecting and sharing, the move to all-digital raises fears about losing access to their favorite titles.
